newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jan natgas prices gain on Midwest demand-NGC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jan natgas prices gain on Midwest demand-NGC.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices climbed to record levels again in January, helped by increased heating demand in the upper Midwest and continued strength on the West Coast, Natural Gas Clearinghouse (NGC) said Tuesday.

U.S. spot gas prices for January averaged $3.96 per million British thermal units, up 26 cents from December's previous record of $3.70 and the highest average price in the 11-year history of the NGC survey.
Prices into Columbia Gas rose five cents on the month to $3.85, about 60 cents over last year's levels, NGC said in its monthly survey.
Most Gulf pipes gained five to 25 cents for the month and stood 40 to 80 cents over year-ago levels.

But the largest monthly gains were seen in Oklahoma, where Panhandle Eastern in Beaver County jumped 60 cents to $4.20, about $2.20 over the same year-ago month. Other Oklahoma pipes saw similar monthly gains and were more than $2.00 over last year's levels.
Sales into El Paso Natural Gas in west Texas averaged $4.05, up 35 cents for the month and $2.10 above last year.

Prices represent NGC estimates of the median price for one month spot transactions at the indicated receipt points. The estimates are based upon quotes by industrial end-users and local distribution companies, NGC said.
